5. Paresh Narayan Choudhury died leaving behind 2 sons, Pronab Narayan Choudhury and Pobitra.Narayan Choudhury and widow Shushayna Debi. The heirs of Paresh Narayan Choudhury started a rent case being Rent Case No.551 of 1956 under Section 48 of the B.T. Act against the Naser Hossain for realization of arrear rents. The suit was contested by Md. Nesar Hossain which was decreed in terms of compromise. Decree Execution Case No 8 of 1957 was started and Nesar Hossain Chowdhury paid total rent of the suit property through chalan dated 26.3.1957 and 9.4.1957. The Collector of Pabna District for realization of rent started a Revenue Sale Case being No.12662 of 1958 for 'Ka' Schedule land wherein Nesar Hossain contested the case and filed an application to recognize him as a tenant. Since Nesar Hossain was in possession of the property by purchase, the Collector of Pabna District by his order dated 27.4.1962 exonerated Nesar Hossain from the responsibility of rent on considering his prayer and the suit property was released in his favour. Nesar Hossain at the time of S.A. settlement recorded his name as per his documents, however, due to conspiracy of some unscrupulous employees of the settlement department `Ka' and Kha Schedule lands were wrongly recorded as a result PRR Khatian Nos. 249(ka) and 257/2 were published in the name of landlords, Pronab Naryan Choudhury and Pobitra Narayan Choudhury. However, both the schedules land at the time of final publication of S.A. record neither recorded in the name of Nesar Hossain, Pronab Narayan Choudhury and Pobitra Narayan Choudhury, nor in the name of the Government. Therefore, there was no record of 'Ka' and 'Kha' Schedules land, Md.Nesar Hossain while learn to know about the facts of the record of Ka and Kha Schedule lands filed an application under Section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SA&T) before the Joint Deputy Commissioner, Revenue Court, which was registered being Case No. 35/1964-65. The Joint Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Pabna on receipt of the case records ordered to inquire into the matter and to submit a report by the then S.D.O., Pabna Sadar, Pabna by 17.6.1965. The SDO, Pabna Sadar submitted the report stating that Nesar Hossain has right and title over the Ka and Kha Schedules land. In that report it was also pointed out that Ka and Kha Schedule lands neither acquired, nor it was recorded in the Khas Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government. In that report the SDO, Pabna also recommended to settle the same in favour of Md.Nesar Hossain as tenant recognizing his documents and possession. Thereafter, the Joint Deputy Commissioner, Pabna after final hearing on 30.6.1965 under the provisions of SA&T Act recognized Nesar Hossain as tenant of Ka and Kha Schedule lands and ordered to open and prepare a Khatian in his name for realization of rent. Accordingly S.A. Khatian No. 257 was opened in the name Nesar Hossain and in the year 1363 B.S. Nesar Hossain paid rent in favour of the Government and obtained rent receipts. 

 "Ka" schedule land as described in the schedule of the suit along with others property was rightly recorded as Lakharaj property of Joykali Bigraha in D.S. khatian No. 248, Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur of Natore was the Shebait of Joykali Bigraha whose name was recorded as Shebait in the C.S. record of right. However, Emperor of India was the superior landlord of the suit property. The C.S. Khatian No. 247 of No. 12 Haludchar Mouza under Natore P.S. of District-Rajshahi was also recorded as 'niskar' where in total 30.69 acres of land was in 8 Plots previous Plot No. 314 of Khatian No. 248 measuring .05 acres of land was Halot for the use of general people. Plot No. 316 of the said Khatian measuring 0.53 acres of land was unused land wherein there was a temple in 03 acres of land. Plot No. 318 of the aforesaid Khatian and Mouza also 11.02 acres of land as Debuttar pond on the said Plot. 0.42 acres of land was a jungle. Plot No. 337 was also a Halot which was used for general public. In Plot No. 317 the 1.32 acres of land was a garden. Before the time of C.S record there was a temple of Joykalimata Bigrah, which are very old temple of the locality. Many worshippers perform their worship duties and thereafter they left the portrait of Bigraha in the ponds water. The worshippers of the temple used to come from others locality and use the water of pond from the time of establishment of the temple. The water of the ponds also used for performing Puja Archana of the Bigrah. Besides it aboriginals resided on the bank of the pond also use the pond's water for their personal purpose. There is a pathway adjacent to the temple which went away towards the village, which was developed by the government. The local aboriginal also cultivate the land of Plot Nos. 316, 321, 337 and 317. They also spent the usufruct of the properties for Puja of the Bigraha. The Pond's name is Marami and the aboriginal people use the same. The aboriginal use their local language although there is no words and letters in writing to write the language of the aboriginal, however, they tried to use the same only in their verbal language. The life style and culture of the aboriginal peoples recognize their cultural heritage. The government of erstwhile East Pakistan published Dacca Gazette in 1963 and 1964 recognizing them as aboriginal peoples and got facilities of Section 97 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and became the tenants under the government. Some of them came from Rajshahi area and settled there. Although some got the landed property, however, their properties were not saved from the hand of some local greedy persons. Some people also left the locality due to disterbance of the local people. Very recent master Shamol, a student of Class-V was killed by some miscreants which is the glaring instance of torture by the local peoples upon the aboriginal peoples. Now the government of Bangladesh has come to save the aboriginal people from the cruelty of the local peoples. There is a project for development of oboriginals which is under active consideration to save them. The total land of C.S. Khatian 248 belonged to Joykalimata Bigraha as the property of Niskar Debuttar property. The suit property at the time of S.A. settlement was recorded in the Kash  Khatian No. 1 in the name of the government. The plaintiff never owned and possessed the suit property. The plaintiff is a stranger and out skier people of locality. He has no right over the suit property. The plaintiff is the resident of Shibgonj P.S. under Bogra District. He was an influential high official of T&T department, who are very expert to influence and made high-handed for doing many bad occurrence and instance for his personal gain. Plaintiff's father Syed Mokkaram Hossain Chowdhury was a Munsif, Pabna in 1950. Plaintiff's father Syed Mokkaram Hossain Chowdhury was the presiding officer of the Munsif Court wherein. Rent Suit No. 551 of 1956 Hof Nesar Hossain was disposed of. There is a signature as Munsif of Syed Mokkaram Hossein Chowdhury in the judgment and decree of the above suit. The father of the plaintiff although was not local people, but with the help of some local peoples tried to grab the suit property by making conspiracy, and accordingly he created some forged, concocted and illegal papers and documents. Kurmar Birandra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait had no power and authority to settle the suit property permanently by estingushing the right title of the Deity's in the name of Paresh Narayan Chowhury or anybody else. In fact he had never made any settlement of the land in favour of Paresh Narayan Chowdhury. The deed of Kabuliyat being No. 7064 of 1943 in the name of the plaintiffs vendor is not original but allegedly a certified copy of forged, concocted and ante dated document only. The plaintiff also obtained some forged rent receipts in pursuance to the so called judgment and decree of the Rent Suit. They allegedly compromised the execution case treating the suit property as their own property only to procured rent receipt although the property in question was `niskar' property of deity. There is no provision in the Bengal Tenancy Act to fix rent upon the aforesaid 'niskar' property. The plaintiff created the aforesaid papers and documents in the name of House Rent Case on compromise decree and procured rent-receipts only to grab the property. The S.A. and P.R.R records of right never stands in the name of the plaintiff, however, he managed to create false, fabricated and baseless S.A and P.R.R records in the name Nesar Hossain, the vendor of the plaintiff and thereafter the plaintiff was/ is never in possession of the suit property. The plaintiff, according to the statements of the plaint never rear fish in the pond and cleared the pond. Nesar Hoasain was not the resident of Marami village nor he resides with his family in the same village. Paresh Narayan Chowdhury has no rent receiving interest under the Bengal Tenancy Act, therefore, he has no right and authority to settle the tenant in the suit property. In the Kabuliyat dated 29.1.1943 there is no statement that Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bhadur settled the suit property in favour of Paresh Narayan Chowdhury for legal necessity of deity nor the plaintiff has stated the aforesaid facts in the previous case, thus the plaintiffs above mentioned statement is barred by the principle of estoppel. S.A. record of rights published and allegedly corrected by an order of Joint Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) vide Mutation Case No. 35 of 64-65 is totally false and fabricated. On query it is detected that there is no existence of Mutation Case No 35 of 1964-65, hence, if any papers submit by the plaintiff that most be forged, concocted and manufactured. The Joint Deputy Commissioner, Revenue has got no power, legally and lawful authority to open the holding in the name of the plaintiffs vendor Nesar Hossain over the Government Khas Khatian land. Therefore, through in any proceedings if obtained any order in pursuance of the proceeding those papers are illegal, void and ab initio. The plaintiff created the papers and documents only to grab the suit property and while came to take over the possession of the suit property forcefully then the local peoples and worshippers of the deity resisted the plaintiff and their men for which the plaintiff was not able to take possession of the property. The plaintiff being unable to take possession at that time disclosed the information of the proprietorship to the local peoples and threatened to take possession anyhow and in that information the defendant inquired the matter and filed an application before the concerned authority. The authority concern inquired the matter and found that the plaintiff created forged and fabricated documents and started the Misc. Case No. 11 of 1996 and after hearing the parties the defendant No. 3 with his opinion sent the case record to  the Deputy Commissioner for necessary order. The Deputy Commissioner Pabna after due consideration of all the events and circumstances of the case rightly  by an order cancelled the mutation of the plaintiff and directed to the authority to revive the previous record of rights in the name of the Government. Hence, the plaintiffs suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

Since the deity has some other properties with the suit property, and as such, the shebait of deity settled the 'Ka.' schedule property in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury. Thereafter Paresh Narayan Choudhury inducted tenant Nesar Hossain as middle interest owner for which Paresh Narayan Choudhury collected rent from Nesar Hossain, thereafter, he paid rent to the deity as a superior landlord, but deity was exempted from paying any rent to the Emperor of India. After the enactment of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act previous system was abolished and in place of superior landlord, state became the owner of all the lands. Therefore, the Government got the right to realize the rent, and as such, by operation of law the tenant became the owner of the property. Hence, as under tenant Nesar Hossain was the owner and possessor of the Ka schedule land by dint of Amalnama dated 22nd Awsin 1351. Thereafter, Nesar Hossain through his legally constituted attorney sold the suit property in favour of the plaintiff. After purchase of the property the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the suit property within the knowledge of the local peoples and he also cultivated the ponds by rearing fish for his personal use. But the Court below without considering the above facts and legal proposition regarding the suit property took an erronous view, dismissing the suit which is liable to be set aside in law. In respect of Kha and Ga schedule lands the Court below in the impugned judgment did not discuss any material evidence regarding title but dismissed the suit as a whole. Therefore, without the specific finding and decision of the trial Court in respect of Kha and Ga schedule properties the impugned judgment and decree cannot be sustained in law. Before pertaining his submission he took us through the impugned judgment and pointed that the trial Court although opined that there is no necessity for discussing about the right, title and possession of Kha and Ga schedule of the suit property and as such, erred in facts and law, however, committed a serious miscarriage of justice dismissing the suit as a whole. Although none of the contesting defendants claimed the Kha and Ga schedule land. As such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside and he prays for allowing the appeal. 

 29. Now, the 1st legal issue is as to whether a Shebait can transfer any property of deity permanently or give Pattan year to year basis. The plaintiff in his plaint admitted that Ka schedule property was the property of deity Joykalimata Thakurani. He further admitted that D.S. record of right was correctly published in the name of deity showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait. According to him Paresh Narayan Choudhury took Pattan by executing Kabuliyat in favour of Kumark Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur by registered Kabuliyat dated 29:11.1943 which is Ext.3. On perusal of Ext.3 it transpires that it is an unilateral Kabuliyat without supporting any Patta or Dakhila issued by the Shebait as representative of the deity. From the practice and customs at that time without Patta and Dakhila unilateral Kabuliyat is not a acceptable document in the eye of law in respect of settlement of any property by the landlord in favour of Raiyat far away to accept the same from a Shebait of a deity. Moreso, it is pertinent to mention that nothing is found in the recital of the Kabuliyat that the property in question was settled by the Shebait for the legal necessity of the Deity. The plaintiff has claimed the title of the "Ka" schedule suit land in question through his vendor Nesar Hossain who purportedly got the same from Paresh Narayan Chowdhury who also got the same by executing a Kabuliyat in favour of the Shebait of Deity namely Birendra Kumar Nath Roy Bahadur. On perusal of the recital of the Kabuliyat in question, it divulged that the executent of Kabuliyat not only included the property of Deity but also included the land property wherein temple is situated. Accordingly the Poresh Narayan and Nesar Hossain the vendors of the plaintiff also transferred the same property to the plaintiff without any correction or rectification. But it is very interesting that the plaintiff although claimed the property through the aforementioned deed exhibit 16 dated 28.8.1965 and the Kabuliyat in question exhibit-3 but in the plaint and in his testimonies P.W. 1 stand corrected the recital of the Kabuliyat and deed in question stating that 03 decimals land wherein temple is situated never settled in favour of the vendor of the plaintiff. According to the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act landlord can settle any property to Raiyat and Raiyat can settle the property to under Raiyat, but nowhere in the Act there is a provision that Shebait of Deity can settle the Debuttar property to any Raiyat giving right of transper as per provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Moreso, property in question surely belonged to Deity not Shebait, so he is not landlord although has got some responsibility only to look after the property as managerial capacity. Therefore, we are of the view that the claim of settlement in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury through unileteral kabuliyat and so on Paresh Narayan Choudhury to Nesar Hossain and to the plaintiff was nothing but a paper transaction without any legal sanction, recognition and basis of title. It is a settled maxim of law that without proving his title deed in accordance with law, by filing some secondary evidence none can claim any title by dint of secondary evidence which are inadmissible in law. The doccuments in question neither produced in original nor proved in accordance with law. Some other private documents were exhibited in violation of provisions of section 63, 64, 65, 66, and 67 of the Evidence Act, a party producing such documents is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution. Even those documents exhibited in trial but the court is to be satisfied as to its execution. 

 31. Mr. Siddique very humbly and candidly has submitted that after enactment of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act Paresh Narayan Chowdhury and Nesar Hossain by operation of Law they became tenants under the Government and as such, the plaintiff through his vendors became the tenant under the Government. Now Government cannot deny the title, possession and record of rights which stand in the name of the plaintiff. To examine and consider the above mentioned legal proposition we have meticulously examined the various provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. On scrutiny the provisions of law it appears that most important feature of the suit land must be discussed which comes into effect after insertion of Section 10A in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. For the reference and convenience of discussion we may quote the Section 10A of the said Act, which runs as follows.

 (5) The arrears of rent and cesses realisable by a Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee from a -tenant under the provision of this section shall be recoverable as a public demand and the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee may apply to the Certificate Officer in the prescribed manner for the recovery of any such arrears under the provisions of the Bengal Public demands Recovery Act, 1913. 

 32. According to the provisions of Section 10A of the said Act it is found that all Debuttar property must he managed, controlled and maintained in accordance with the aforementioned provisions of law. Here we must express our view that the 'Ka' schedule suit property of the present case admittedly was/is a Debuttar property since its inception which was correctly recorded in the name of Deity at the time of preparation of D.S. record of rights during the colonial regime of British showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait who was the donor of the property. It further appears from the pleadings of the suit, from the recital of exhibit 3 and deposition of P.W.1 herein he admitted that Ka schedule land was /is a Deity's property. It is further admitted facts that there is a temple with Deity and a big pond from which it is apparent that there was/is nothing cultivable and arable land. Ka schedule total land is occupied by the big pond, temple and Pathway of the temple, so how it would be settled for cultivation to a Raiyat which happened in this case. Since from the time of D.S, record of rights the Ka schedule land belonged to Deity as Debuttar property which never comes within the ambit of the settlement as per the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act or thereafter, by operation of law of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 Moreso, the defendant Government including the period of the erstwhile East Pakistan Government have failed to produce any notification or assessment-roll in respect of the suit land which admittedly a debuttar property, hence, as per provisions of Section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, unless Government take over the possession of the property as provided in the law none but only Deity is the owner and possessor of the Ka schedule land and as such, Shebait will act as representative of the Government. 

 D.W. 1 in his deposition stated that Joykalimata Thakurani is the owner of the suit properties as per D.S. Record of rights where in Mr. Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur was the Shabait but on perusal of the materials on record it transpires that Deity's properties only belongs to schedule Ka of the Suit Nos. 8 and 9 of 2003. The plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 9 of 2003 to prove his case did not adduce any documentary evidence except oral, from which it appears that the plaintiff of Title Sun No. 9 of 2003 has failed to prove their locus standi to file and prosecute the suit. Although it is admitted fact that the schedule No. Ka of Title Suit No. 9 of 2003 is the property of Deity, which also admitted by the P.W. 1 Jamshed Hossain Chowdhury. So, it is apparent that the Deity has had the right, title over the Ka schedule land as per the D.S. Khatian and admission of the plaintiffs of T.S. No. 8 of 2003 unless Government take over the property as per the provision of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. Since we are affirming the judgment and decree so far it relates to other Suit No. 8 of 2003 hence, the right title of the Deity's is affirmed subject to provisions of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950.
